findings.amended: Same fix, plus: the skill writes each decision into DESIGN_NOTES with a status line ([shipped]/[partial]/[planned: roadmap-id]) and adds a roadmap.yaml entry. The AGENTS.md bullet is written only by the delivering change's docs step. Migrate existing planned bullets out of AGENTS.md once.
findings.conflicts: Today's AGENTS.md carries unbuilt registry bullets (Rival, Offices, Channels, Orbital Pass and others); they must move to DESIGN_NOTES or the new test (S6A-07) fails. Consistent with the design-notes skill's own coherence assessment, which can stay.
findings.note: This is the generator of the drift, so fixing the procedure is cheaper than any after-the-fact check. It adds no file and removes no gate.

findings.amended: Also assert engines/.nvmrc against package.json in the docs-truth test. Keep one README sentence, 'versions: see package.json'. Mark HF as 'planned, unpinned' in DESIGN_NOTES, not AGENTS.
findings.conflicts: AGENTS.md currently names TS 7.0.2 and 6.0.2; the test in S6A-07 should check these against package.json instead of deleting the mention outright.
findings.note: Single source of truth plus a loud check is the right shape. No new layer.

findings.amended: Drop CVE IDs and the 'include table in design' rule as proposed. Keep `npm audit` as a manual or CI step outside verify, and keep the Node pin as one line plus .nvmrc.
findings.conflicts: The rule lives in openspec/config.yaml context and is repeated in proposals, so remove it there (S6A-06) rather than in README only. Do not cite this as a change in README/AGENTS.
findings.note: Unverifiable authority text is worse than none for agents. Low risk, small edit.

findings.amended: Endorse notes/inbox.md as the ONE new file, but the dispositions table lives in DESIGN_NOTES as an appendix of one-line rows (raw ref, integrated->section, open->roadmap id, rejected->why), not in a second file. Skill step 0 reads the inbox; inbox must be empty or fully dispositioned at the end of a skill run. Disposition the camera-capture and zoom items right now.
findings.conflicts: Skill currently forbids removing the raw dump from DESIGN_NOTES; edit the skill, and the 'three-agent coherence assessment' should check the inbox is empty. Raw dump lines currently in DESIGN_NOTES need a one-time migration.
findings.note: Gives the owner a safe dump spot with a lifecycle, which matches how they actually work. It is a staging area that gets emptied, so it cannot drift the way a mirror would. Still, an inbox that is never emptied is the failure mode, so the test should fail loudly if inbox.md has an entry older than the last skill run.

findings.amended: Owner table lives as a short 'Where facts live' table at the top of DESIGN_NOTES (not a new file). Numbers (epoch count, verify budget, task limits) are asserted by the docs-truth test against code constants or one parameter table; prose copies become pointers.
findings.conflicts: Must not collide with P1/P5: the 7-epoch ladder is a default, data-driven, so docs should say 'default arc, see registry' and never a hard count. AGENTS.md text 'default 7-Epoch arc' is acceptable once pointing to the owner.
findings.note: Correct diagnosis. A table with no check is one more thing to drift, so tie the table to at least a few mechanical assertions (budget numbers, ladder length vs default pack).

findings.amended: Cut context to a stub of under 1.5k words (invariants, rules a proposal must obey, pointers). Move the roadmap to openspec/roadmap.yaml (see S6B-04), not roadmap.md. Add a word budget assertion on the context string so it cannot regrow silently.
findings.conflicts: Merge with S6B-04 so there is a single roadmap file, not roadmap.md plus roadmap.yaml. The spec-rules from S6B-01 must still be injected via context rules, so the stub must keep those. The 'check DESIGN_NOTES before proposing' rule in AGENTS.md stays.
findings.note: Big token and staleness win with no loss of review gates. Roadmap status should be derived (archive folders), not stored, to avoid the stale tag problem recurring.

findings.amended: Keep the test, under 100 ms. Scope: AGENTS.md and src/*/AGENTS.md backticked identifiers and npm scripts must resolve; no <!-- planned --> escape hatch inside AGENTS (planned content lives only in DESIGN_NOTES per S6A-01), only an explicit short allowlist file for generic words. Add three cheap checks: README versions equal package.json; AGENTS/README/src/tests contain no OpenSpec change id or 'Change NN' (the existing citation rule is currently unenforced); DESIGN_NOTES sections have a status marker whose roadmap id resolves in roadmap.yaml. Add soft word-count budgets that fail at a ceiling.
findings.conflicts: S6A-07 as written allows planned blocks in AGENTS, contradicting S6A-01 and R6A1. Citation rule: planned markers cite roadmap ids, so they may appear only in DESIGN_NOTES/openspec.
findings.note: Strongest item in the set: a loud failure beats a review. Risk is false positives on identifiers, so start narrow (PascalCase, snake_case reducer names, npm scripts) and widen.

findings.amended: Reject the three-new-layer shape. Pillars P1-P5 and a 'Rules spine' section (numbered R1.., each with status shipped/planned/revisable, per P5) live in DESIGN_NOTES with the index table. No docs/decisions ADR folder: the rationale for an accepted/rejected decision lives where OpenSpec already puts it, the change's design.md Decisions section, with the register in reviews/ as archived history. No docs/START.md (see R6A2). Hardening batch and prerequisites become roadmap.yaml entries.
findings.conflicts: Compatible with the design-notes skill (which already targets DESIGN_NOTES). docs/spine.md would sit beside DESIGN_NOTES as a second design doc and invite divergence; ADRs duplicate design.md. If the owner wants the spine on its own page, make it a section whose heading is stable, still one file.
findings.note: Yes, spine + ADRs + START is one layer too many for a solo owner. The class-to-home idea is the valuable part and is kept as the 'Where facts live' table. AGENTS.md shipped-only plus a link is endorsed.

findings.amended: Endorse the consumer scenario but scope it: a requirement whose Purpose is persistence, logging, or a pipeline MUST have a scenario from user-visible trigger to observable consumer, and design.md MUST list producer and consumer call sites in non-test code. Add as a rule in openspec/config.yaml rules. Backfill only lab Save and telemetry via the hardening spec-delta changes, not all specs.
findings.conflicts: Overlaps R6B3 and G1: use this as the one mechanism and drop R6B3. openspec validate --strict may reject unknown requirement fields, so keep this as a scenario plus a design.md section, not a new spec syntax. Aligned with the 4-6 task rule replacement since the scenario needs a task.
findings.note: Addresses the true failure (features compliant yet inert) at spec time, where it is cheapest. Adds a rule, not a file.

findings.amended: Same. Also let the audit Subagent B check that every register finding which contradicts an archived requirement has a MODIFIED delta in some roadmap entry (specs_modified field).
findings.conflicts: Uses OpenSpec spec deltas as designed. Interacts with roadmap.yaml: specs_modified keeps it traceable.
findings.note: Keeps specs true by construction, the best anti-drift form, and uses the existing workflow.

findings.amended: G1 endorse (run the real entry point, name producer/consumer call sites). G2 and G4 endorse, but add them as named axes inside the existing Adversarial reviewer (post-change #1) and per-subtask Subagent A, and G3 inside Performance (#3), so the briefs are fuller rather than new agents. G5: endorse as a short defect ledger (reviews/ledger.md, one line per post-merge defect with the axis that should have caught it); every row must end in a new test or an edited gate brief, else it is only a log. G6: replace 'grep each SHALL' (grep cannot verify behaviour) with a scenario-to-test traceability check done by the Code Adherence reviewer, plus S6B-01 for end-to-end. Also move the gate briefs out of root AGENTS.md into .agents/skills/uplift-review-gates/SKILL.md so one copy feeds all gates, leaving a pointer in AGENTS.md.
findings.conflicts: The gate text is currently in AGENTS.md section 1-3 and the design-notes skill; moving it is a pure relocation, no gate removed. A skill location is already mandated (.agents/skills). A throwing-input test per entry point (G4) adds tests under the <3s unit budget; keep them tiny.
findings.note: Adds scrutiny without reducing any gate, which matches the owner's stated preference. G5 is the only item that creates a new artifact, so give it a forcing function. Do not count these as extra gate tasks inside tasks.md.

findings.amended: Adopt openspec/roadmap.yaml, but simplify: array order IS the order; fields {id, title, depends_on, specs_modified, status: planned|parked|proposed}. Archived and active are derived from openspec/changes/archive and openspec/changes folders, never stored. The architecture test asserts ids unique, deps resolve, every dep appears earlier in the array (valid topological order, replacing topo-sort-with-slot-tiebreak), archived folders are all present as ids, and at most one active. `roadmap:next` prints the first non-archived entry whose deps are archived. Drop `source` and `slot`; findings cite roadmap ids from the register instead.
findings.conflicts: If no YAML parser is already a dependency, store as roadmap.json or reuse the existing parser used for config. Letter suffixes: existing changes (05b, 05c, 09a) must keep their ids. Ids appear only in openspec/ and DESIGN_NOTES per the citation rule; DESIGN_NOTES markers must resolve here (S6A-07). Replaces roadmap in config.yaml (S6A-06).
findings.note: Roadmap as data answers 'what next' mechanically, which is what agents need. Deriving status avoids the stale-tag defect. Fewer stored fields means fewer drifts, while P5 stays served by trivial edits to a list.

findings.amended: Keep the intent: one task = one green reviewable commit, at most 3 source files plus tests, docs updates inside the feature task that changes the module, one closing review task, unplanned fixes recorded as 'x.y-fix'. Replace the count cap with: a change with a task whose output no earlier task depends on is a split point; more than 8 tasks or more than 3 layers requires the proposal to name its split or justify it, enforced by audit Subagent B rather than a hard fail.
findings.conflicts: Rewrite in all places: AGENTS.md section 1 Subagent B, openspec/config.yaml, and tasks guidance, so only one owner states it (S6A-05). The 6-subagent post-change gate and per-subtask 2-subagent review are untouched. Keep the 'docs check' guard so docs-in-feature-task is still enforced by test:arch.
findings.note: A size rule measures the right thing and docs-with-code reduces lag drift. A hard numeric ceiling invites gaming, hence a justify-or-split rule with an agent check.

findings.amended: Adopt the change plan as roadmap.yaml entries with status planned, each naming depends_on and specs_modified, covering the ownerless slots (launch validation, telemetry wiring, minimal audio, spec amendments). Do not pre-write OpenSpec proposals; they stay /opsx-propose time work so the DESIGN_NOTES check precedes them.
findings.conflicts: The finding says 'change_plan list in this file' but S6-recs-routes.json has no such list; the source must be located or regenerated before use. Conflicts with P5 if treated as frozen, so mark planned entries revisable. Citation rule: ids stay in openspec/ and DESIGN_NOTES.
findings.note: Needed so accepted work has an owner, but entries are cheap list rows. Pre-proposing 30 changes would go stale immediately.

routes.amended: Markers go on DESIGN_NOTES numbered sections only; AGENTS.md is shipped-only so needs no marker. Markers are [shipped], [partial], [planned: roadmap-id] and resolve against roadmap.yaml. Same test as S6A-07.
routes.conflicts: Overlaps S6A-01 and S6A-07 (one mechanism, not three). R6A1's AGENTS-with-[planned]-block variant conflicts with shipped-only.
routes.note: The core of the fix: marker makes planned vs shipped visible and the test makes it loud.

routes.amended: Keep: size budgets (AGENTS.md under about 900 words, DESIGN_NOTES per-section ceiling, config context under 1.5k) enforced by word-count test; versions only in package.json; notes/inbox.md; index table at top of DESIGN_NOTES. Reject: docs/START.md (AGENTS.md is already the auto-loaded start page and a second index drifts), splitting DESIGN_NOTES into docs/design/*, docs/decisions ADRs.
routes.conflicts: Splitting DESIGN_NOTES breaks the design-notes skill and every rule naming DESIGN_NOTES.md; ADRs duplicate design.md.
routes.note: A 400-word START is a copy of AGENTS.md plus pillars. Put the pillars at the top of DESIGN_NOTES and make AGENTS.md link them. Budgets that fail loudly are the useful part.

routes.amended: As S6B-04 (array order topological, derived status, trimmed fields). Prose descriptions stay in proposal.md.
routes.conflicts: Replaces the roadmap section of config.yaml; consistent with S6A-06.

routes.amended: Adopt `npm run smoke` as a post-change gate step run by the G1 reviewer and the Performance reviewer, outside verify like eval:ai. Use system Chromium or a dev-only Playwright dependency, cap runtime, and make assertions deterministic (fixed seed, 600 frames, forced throw contained, Save then reload). Document in AGENTS.md only once it exists.
routes.conflicts: Offline-first: Playwright browser download is a one-time install, document it. Must not enter verify (budget under 5 s). Depends on lab Save and frame guard existing (hardening changes).
routes.note: This is an added gate that proves features really work, which is what the owner favours. It is the only way to catch the inert-feature class mechanically.

routes.amended: Fold into S6B-01: scenario plus design.md call-site list for persistence/pipeline requirements only.
routes.conflicts: Would add a free-form line on every requirement across all specs, which openspec validate may not accept and which needs ongoing upkeep. A symbol grep proves existence, not consumption.
routes.note: A drift-prone per-requirement annotation. The scoped consumer scenario gives the same protection with no new syntax.

doc_shape: Keep: AGENTS.md (shipped-only, under ~900 words, links onward), README.md, section AGENTS/README pairs. DESIGN_NOTES.md gains a top block: pillars P1-P5, 'Where facts live' owner table, index table (section, status shipped/partial/planned+roadmap id), a numbered Rules spine (R1.., status, revisable), and a dispositions appendix; no raw text. New: notes/inbox.md (owner dumps, emptied by the design-notes skill), openspec/roadmap.yaml (ordered list, depends_on, specs_modified; archived/active derived; roadmap:next), .agents/skills/uplift-review-gates/SKILL.md (the gate briefs moved out of AGENTS.md, with G1-G6 axes), reviews/ledger.md (defect ledger). config.yaml context under 1.5k words (invariants plus S6B-01 spec rule, pointers). Versions only in package.json. One docs-truth test in tests/architecture: identifier resolution, README/package versions, no change ids outside openspec and DESIGN_NOTES, markers resolve to roadmap, word budgets, roadmap DAG. No docs/spine.md, ADRs or START.md.
